title: Webitel WebRTC Recorder
description: Screen recording pipeline: WebRTC sessions → transcoding (ffmpeg) → upload to storage.

panels.title: Active sessions
panels.description: WebRTC recording sessions in progress right now.

panels.title: Transcoding backlog
panels.description: Recordings waiting for or in transcoding (database).

panels.title: Upload backlog
panels.description: Transcoded files waiting for or in upload to storage (database).

panels.title: Oldest pending job
panels.description: Age of the oldest job in the database. Growing value means the pipeline is stuck or can't keep up.

panels.title: Lost recordings (range)
panels.description: Jobs dropped after max retries in the selected time range: the recording was deleted and never reached storage.

panels.title: Temp disk free
panels.description: Free space on the cache dir filesystem (worst instance). Raw tracks and mp4 files are buffered there until uploaded.

panels.title: Pipeline throughput
panels.description: Per minute. In a healthy system all three lines overlap; a gap means files accumulate between stages.

panels.title: Transcoding attempts / min
panels.description: error = will be retried, dropped = max retries reached, recording lost.

panels.title: Transcoding speed (x realtime)
panels.description: Recorded media duration / transcoding time. Below 1 a single worker is slower than realtime: with N workers the instance sustains roughly N × speed concurrent recordings.

panels.title: Transcoding workers
panels.description: Busy constantly at capacity = add workers/CPU (each worker runs one ffmpeg).

panels.title: Upload error ratio
panels.description: Share of failed attempts. Upload errors usually mean the storage service is unavailable.

panels.title: Finished sessions / min
panels.description: Final ICE state at the end of a session. 'failed'/'new'/'checking' — the client never got (or lost) media connectivity.

panels.title: Packet loss
panels.description: network = lost on the wire; in recording = gaps left after NACK retransmits (visible artifacts). Counters are added when a session ends.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (rate(webrtc_recorder_rtp_packets_total{instance=~"$instance", state="lost"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (kind) (rate(webrtc_recorder_rtp_packets_total{instance=~"$instance", state="received"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (kind) (rate(webrtc_recorder_rtp_packets_total{instance=~"$instance", state="lost"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum by (kind) (rate(webrtc_recorder_rtp_packets_total{instance=~"$instance", state="unrecovered"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (kind) (rate(webrtc_recorder_rtp_packets_total{instance=~"$instance", state="received"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: NACK / PLI / ICE disconnects per min
panels.description: PLI = keyframe requests (picture freezes until a keyframe arrives).

panels.title: Selected ICE candidate pair
panels.description: local→remote candidate types of the connected pair. relay = through TURN, srflx = via NAT, host = direct.

panels.title: Inbound media (ended sessions)
panels.description: Bytes are counted when a session ends, so the curve is bursty; use for long-range trends.

panels.title: CPU (service process, without ffmpeg)
panels.description: Cores used by the Go process. ffmpeg runs as child processes and is not included — use node/cAdvisor metrics for total CPU.
